title: Chief of Staff / Executive Assistant to Health Care CEO
description:
About Maniya Health



Maniya Health is a premier, 75-employee multispecialty medical practice in Central New Jersey that has served our community for over 50 years. We were named #920 on the 2026 Inc. 5000 list of America's fastest-growing private companies. We are looking for a high-capacity EA / Operations Manager to serve as the strategic right hand to our CEO.



Position Overview



The primary purpose of this role is to make the CEO's life easier. Everything else follows from that.



You will take work off the CEO's plate entirely — not by executing tasks he hands you, but by owning outcomes so completely that he stops thinking about them. Beyond direct executive support, you will manage the intersection of healthcare operations, HR, talent, IT, facilities, and project delivery. This is a senior role for someone who owns the result, not the checklist.



This is a role with real scope and real autonomy, working directly with a physician-MBA CEO at a practice growing fast enough to make the Inc. 5000. You will learn every aspect of how an innovative medical practice runs, under close mentorship, with genuine room to grow as we expand. What you build here, you own.



Structure



Reports directly to the CEO. No direct reports to start — you influence and coordinate across departments through ownership and follow-through rather than formal authority. Scope may grow as the practice does.



Schedule



Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM US Eastern Time. Remote. Full-time and exclusive — no concurrent employment or client work during scheduled hours. May require additional hours for urgent issues such as a system outage or a same-day provider gap.



Your First 30 Days



Training on all Practice workflows. Inbox and calendar management, provider scheduling and PTO end to end, and closing the open vendor loops that currently sit with the CEO.



Responsibilities

1. Executive Support — The Core of the Role

Full Lifecycle Ownership: You are the final destination for anything assigned to you. When the CEO CCs you on an
 or delegates a project, you own it until it's done. He should never have to follow up or wonder about status.

Inbox Management: Oversee the general practice inboxes, routing information as appropriate. Once trust is established, you will manage the CEO's inbox — triaging, drafting responses, flagging what genuinely needs him, handling the rest.

Calendar & Anticipation: Manage the CEO's calendar with foresight, including professional and personal logistics such as travel and events. Adjust for time zones, seasonal shifts like Daylight Savings, and personal commitments — holidays, celebrations, errands — without being prompted.

Closing Open Loops: Many of our vendors and partners don't respond, or agree to something and go quiet. Today the CEO carries those loops in his head. Your job is to take them off his plate entirely — own the follow-up cadence, escalate when needed, close every loop.

Representing the CEO: Attend vendor and partner meetings on his behalf. Take detailed notes, capture action items and owners, circulate the summary, drive follow-ups to closure. You are a polite but firm representative, ensuring team deadlines are met.



2. Project Management

General Project Ownership: Projects come planned and unplanned. A provider gives notice and hundreds of patients need rescheduling. A new AI phone system has bugs to identify, report, and verify as fixed. A service line needs standing up. You take the goal, break it into steps, identify who does what, and drive it to completion — surfacing risks early and never letting it stall silently.

Vendor Sourcing: Research and source vendors for software, hardware, and services. Run comparisons, gather quotes, check references, present options with a recommendation.

Implementation & Closure: Own implementations end to end — configuration, testing, staff training, go-live. Identify bugs, log them with the vendor, and follow up until they are actually fixed. A ticket submitted is not a ticket resolved.

Renewals & Contracts: Track renewal dates, licenses, and service agreements so nothing auto-renews unnoticed or lapses unexpectedly.



3. Provider Scheduling & Coordination

End-to-End Ownership: Manage the full lifecycle of provider scheduling, vacations, PTO, and CME across approximately 40 providers. You are the final auditor — 100% accuracy across EHR and tracking systems before anything reaches the CEO's desk.

Visiting Specialists: Several providers are specialists who come in one day a week from their own practices. You coordinate directly with their offices — confirming schedules, managing changes and cancellations, keeping templates accurate, making sure their day runs smoothly on site.



4. HR, Talent & Employee Lifecycle

Recruiting & Hiring: Lead sourcing, job posting, resume screening, interview scheduling, and coordination with hiring managers. Build the pipeline before a seat opens.

Onboarding & Offboarding: Own onboarding end to end — paperwork, system access, training coordination, day-one readiness. Same rigor on exit: final paperwork, access removal, equipment return.

Talent & Compliance: Coordinate performance reviews, track training and credentialing, monitor license and certification expirations. You don't just send documents — you manage the completion rate, ensuring every signature is captured and filed.



5. Facilities, IT & Office Administration

Account Management: Provision accounts for new hires across all systems; de-provision immediately on departure. Access sprawl is a compliance risk, and closing it is your responsibility.

IT Support & Continuity: Handle everyday requests — password resets, access issues, device and printer problems, basic troubleshooting. Know the failover procedures and execute them; if the phone system goes down, route to the backup and notify the team. Know what you can fix and what needs a vendor — escalate fast, then own the follow-up.

Facilities Issues: When a roof leaks or the HVAC fails, you own it from first report to final invoice. You won't be on site, so you coordinate with our on-the-ground team to get eyes on the problem and confirm the work was done properly. Your part is getting the vendor scheduled — following up daily if that's what it takes — and verifying the bill matches the quote.

Supplies & Equipment: Keep every location stocked — clinical supplies, office supplies, everyday consumables. Nobody should ever tell the CEO we've run out of something.

Purchase Orders, Reimbursements & Refunds: Review, approve, and track POs with a clear record of what was ordered, what arrived, and what it cost. Same for staff reimbursement requests and patient refunds — reviewed, approved, tracked to completion.



6. Operational Oversight

Daily Review: Review checklists and Google Chat spaces daily to identify operational gaps and correct provider scheduling gaps.

Monthly Operational Reviews: Prepare and run them — pull the data, build the deck, identify what moved and what didn't, come with recommendations rather than just numbers.

Process Ownership: Own the recurring administrative and operational processes that keep the practice running. You know which exist, whether they were completed, and where they break down — and you fix them rather than reporting that they broke.

Patient Discharges & RCM: Execute the patient discharge process end to end, with the rigor these documents require. We have a billing manager who owns billing operations; your role is coordination and oversight — confirming revenue cycle processes are running, surfacing issues, following up on anything that stalls.



7. Data & Analysis

Reporting & Dashboards: Use Excel and Google Sheets to turn operational, financial, and clinical quality data into reports that drive decisions. Build, maintain, and present operational KPI dashboards. When something breaks, dig into why and lead the process improvement rather than patching symptoms.

Analyst on New Initiatives: Serve as data analyst on new projects — researching potential service lines, expansion opportunities, and market questions. Gather the data, run the analysis, present findings with a recommendation rather than a data dump.



Key Requirements

Outcome Ownership: You own results, not tasks. You act as your own auditor and catch your own errors before anyone else does. You maintain 100% accuracy in high-stakes repetitive workflows — PTO approvals, provider scheduling, PO tracking. When a project stalls, you feel it personally.

Persistence: Much of this job is making other people do what they said they would — vendors, contractors, partners, internal teams. You follow up five times without becoming apologetic or abrasive.

Reliability: You are a steady, reachable anchor during business hours. If you can't make a commitment — a call, a deadline, a check-in — you say so in advance rather than going quiet. A missed commitment with notice is a scheduling problem; a missed commitment without notice is a trust problem.

Anticipation & Context: You connect the dots without being told, looking ahead at the calendar and environmental factors to adjust proactively. You understand how one change in a physician's schedule ripples through five other systems.

Risk-Based Judgment: In a medical practice, administrative work carries legal and clinical weight. You approach sensitive documentation — patient discharge letters, HR contracts — with extreme rigor and full compliance with US healthcare standards.

30,000 Feet and 2 Feet: You can move between strategic and tactical without losing quality on either — building a KPI dashboard in the morning and chasing a roofer in the afternoon. Both matter, and you stay calm and organized across both.

Technical Fluency: Advanced Excel and Google Workspace — trackers, pivot tables, VLOOKUPs — plus the ability to quickly master new software including EHR and HRIS.



On AI



We use AI tools daily and expect you to. What we care about is whether you direct the tool and verify the output, or hand over your thinking. Be transparent about where you use it.



On Monitoring



Because this role has access to protected health information, all work is performed on monitored systems using Teramind. Every team member with PHI access operates under the same requirements.



To be direct: any attempt to circumvent monitoring — mouse movers, jigglers, activity simulators, or anything similar — ends the engagement immediately. If the schedule or workload isn't working, tell us and we'll fix it.



Qualifications

5–7+ years as a senior EA, Operations Manager, or Chief of Staff

Direct CEO or C-suite support experience is mandatory. You must have supported a CEO or equivalent executive before. This is not a role where you learn executive support on the job.

Mandatory: Deep experience in the US healthcare / medical practice ecosystem

Job longevity is mandatory. We are looking for someone who has held prior roles for multiple years, not a pattern of short stints. If your resume shows several positions under a year, please explain why in your application.

Advanced Excel (pivot tables, VLOOKUPs) and Google Workspace

Working proficiency with Claude, Gemini, and ChatGPT

Proven ability to master internal software (EHR, HRIS) and maintain complex checklists, prioritization, and follow-up with 100% accuracy

Selection Process



Advancing candidates complete a short practical exercise using real operational data. It assesses analytical accuracy, critical thinking, and — most importantly — how you verify your own work.



Final candidates should expect reference checks with prior supervisors, including on attendance and follow-through.

title: Customer Service Representative - Dropshipping in Europe to China - 20+ responses per hour, AI experience (Shopify).
description:
# Customer Service Representative — Shopify Dropshipping 
 Support)



We run multiple Shopify dropshipping stores in Europe and are looking for a reliable Customer Service Representative to join our customer support team.



This is an
 support role. You will handle customer
s, use our templates and workflows, log refunds in Google Sheets, and escalate complex cases when needed.



You MUST already have experience with customer service for dropshipping stores. Experience handling support for multiple stores at the same time is a big advantage.



---



## Main Responsibilities



* Answer customer
s for Shopify dropshipping stores

* Maintain a steady pace of around **20 answered
s per hour**

* Handle order questions, shipping updates, returns, refunds, lost packages, and defective product claims

* Use DeepL to translate Dutch, Polish, and other European customer
s

* Start from the correct pre-written template, but personalize every single reply — customers should never receive an obvious copy-paste answer

* Build and improve your own ChatGPT prompt/template so each
 is written specifically for that customer and their situation

* Handle refund requests using our step-by-step compensation ladder and keep the overall refund percentage as low as possible

* Keep customers calm and satisfied to reduce disputes and escalations

* Log refunds and important cases in Google Sheets

* Check supplier/order information when needed

* Escalate unclear, aggressive, or complex cases through Slack

* Coordinate with another CS team member so work is divided properly



---



## Refunds & Resolution Ladder



Refunds have a direct impact on our margins, so an important part of this role is solving problems properly instead of handing out money by default.



We work with a fixed ladder. You always start at the lowest step:



1. **20% partial refund** — the standard first offer

2. **40% partial refund** — only if the customer declines the first offer and the case justifies it

3. **60% partial refund** — final step, only for serious cases

4. **Return to our supplier in China** — the alternative if the customer does not accept a partial refund



Do not skip steps. Never jump to a higher percentage just because it is faster or easier, and never issue a full refund on your own — those cases go to Slack first.



Every offer must be explained in a friendly, personalized message so the customer feels heard and accepts the solution instead of opening a dispute or chargeback.



---



## Requirements



* Must have experience with CS for Shopify dropshipping stores

* Experience supporting multiple stores is preferred

* Excellent written English

* Strong attention to detail

* Able to follow workflows and templates exactly

* Confident handling refund negotiations and sticking to the compensation ladder

* Able to work at a fast, consistent pace (around 20
s per hour)

* Calm, professional tone with customers

* Comfortable using Gmail, Google Sheets, DeepL, Slack, and ChatGPT

* Comfortable running Hubstaff time tracking during your shifts

* Reliable internet and availability 6 days per week

* Able to work in a coordinated schedule with another CS team member



---



## Performance & Tracking



* We expect around **20
s answered per hour**. With templates, DeepL, and our documented workflows this is very achievable once you know the system.

* Working hours are tracked with **Hubstaff**, which records time and activity during your shift. Hubstaff only runs while you are clocked in on your shift.

* We also look at your **refund rate**: how many cases you manage to resolve at the lowest possible step of the ladder.

* Speed matters, but quality matters too. Wrong or careless replies create disputes, so accuracy comes first.



---



## Languages



You do not need to speak Dutch or other European languages.



We use DeepL, pre-written templates, and documented workflows. You need strong English and the ability to understand the customer issue correctly after translation.



---



## Hours & Compensation



* Part-time to start

* Around 12–18 hours per week

* **Around 2–3 hours per day, 6 days per week**

* More hours possible as workload grows

* **Rate: $4 per hour**

* Payment: weekly via Wise, based on the hours tracked in Hubstaff



The schedule is not fully random/flexible. You will work together with another CS team member, so hours need to be coordinated to avoid overlap and make sure
s are covered properly.



---



## Important



When you start your session, the assigned inbox must be cleared properly. Customer
s should not be left unanswered without a clear reason or escalation.



We are looking for someone reliable, consistent, and long-term.



---



## How To Apply



Please reply with:



1. The word **LIGHTHOUSE** in the subject of your application

2. A short introduction about yourself

3. Your experience with Shopify dropshipping customer service

4. Whether you have handled CS for multiple stores at the same time (include store names / links)

5. Which tools you have used before: Gmail, Shopify, Google Sheets, Slack, DeepL, ChatGPT, Hubstaff, etc.

6. Your time zone and daily availability

7. When you can start

8. A short answer to this question: a customer writes that their product arrived damaged and demands a full refund. How do you handle it?

9. Confirmation that you are comfortable with the $4/hour rate and the 20
s per hour target

10. A screenshot of your internet speed test from speedtest.net



Applications without dropshipping CS experience will not be considered.



Looking forward to working together long-term!

title: Short-Term Rental Property Operations Manager - Full-Time US Hours
description:
HOURS PER WEEK

40



MONTHLY SALARY

USD $1,300-$2,000 per month



JOB OVERVIEW



ABOUT DIVERGENT ESTATES



Divergent Estates is a growing U.S.-based short-term rental management company. We help property owners operate professional, guest-ready vacation rentals across multiple U.S. markets.



We are hiring a long-term, full-time Short-Term Rental Property Operations Manager. Internally, we call this role a Pod Manager.



This is not a general virtual assistant or customer-service-only position. It is an ownership role for someone who can build the operating team around a small group of properties and then manage those properties from A to Z.



HOW THE ROLE STARTS



You will be assigned a small number of target properties before they are fully transitioned to you.



For each property, you will:



- Validate and organize the property information

- Build the primary and backup cleaning team

- Build the local maintenance and specialty-vendor bench

- Document contacts, procedures and escalation paths in Notion

- Configure HostBuddy AI so it can answer routine guest questions

- Review the PriceLabs setup and learn the approved pricing guardrails

- Identify open problems and create a stabilization plan

- Pass a property-readiness review



Once the property passes the readiness review, you will formally accept responsibility for it. Properties will transfer to you one at a time, so you will own the team and operating system you helped build.



WHAT YOU WILL OWN



- Cleaner scheduling, performance, inspections and backup coverage

- Maintenance intake, troubleshooting, vendor dispatch and completion follow-through

- Daytime guest issues that HostBuddy AI cannot resolve

- Proactive owner communication and documented decisions

- Property supplies, recurring services and operational readiness

- Accurate property and vendor information in Notion

- PriceLabs execution within approved company guardrails

- Open tasks from the first report through verified completion

- Operational onboarding for additional properties assigned to your pod



PriceLabs ownership includes monitoring calendar health, minimum-stay rules, orphan gaps, local events and approved overrides. Major pricing strategy and changes outside the approved guardrails require company approval until you complete our internal certification.



✅ REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS



- Excellent spoken and written English

- Confidence making phone calls to U.S.-based cleaners, handymen and vendors

- Experience in short-term rentals, property management, hospitality operations or a comparable operations role

- Strong problem-solving and prioritization under time pressure

- Ability to troubleshoot maintenance issues before sending a vendor

- Clear documentation and disciplined follow-through

- Reliable internet, a quiet workspace and a professional call setup

- Ability to work full time without overlapping full-time employment

- Comfort accepting responsibility for results, not only completing assigned tasks



HELPFUL EXPERIENCE



Experience with any of the following is helpful but not required:



- Hostaway or another property management system

- Breezeway or another cleaning and maintenance platform

- PriceLabs or another revenue-management tool

- Notion, Slack or remote documentation systems

- HostBuddy or another AI guest-messaging system

- Cleaner, handyman or vendor sourcing in unfamiliar markets

- Owner-facing communication



SCHEDULE AND COMPENSATION



This is a full-time remote position with primary coverage during U.S. Central Time business hours. There will be a scheduled weekend rotation. Overnight on-call coverage is handled separately.



The exact working schedule will be confirmed before an offer.



Base compensation is USD $1,300-$2,000 per month from day one, including the initial build-to-own ramp. Placement within the range depends on demonstrated experience, spoken communication, maintenance judgment and ability to operate independently.



We are looking for someone interested in a stable, long-term role with the opportunity to manage a larger portfolio and grow in compensation as performance and responsibility increase.



HOW TO APPLY



Start the first line of your application with the word OWNERSHIP. Applications that do not follow this instruction will not be reviewed.



Please include:



1. Your resume or a summary of your relevant work history

2. A 60-90 second audio or video introduction explaining your relevant experience

3. Your answers to the five questions below



APPLICATION QUESTIONS



1. How many properties, units or active clients have you directly supported? What work did you personally own?



2. Describe a time you sourced a cleaner or maintenance vendor in a market where you had no existing contacts. What did you do and what was the result?



3. A cleaner cancels three hours before a same-day guest check-in. Walk us through your first 15 minutes and your next steps.



4. Describe a maintenance problem you helped troubleshoot before sending a vendor. What questions did you ask and how did you d
 what to do?



5. Which property-management, pricing or operations systems have you used? Explain what you personally managed inside those systems.



Shortlisted candidates will complete a paid, role-specific exercise before the final interview.

title: Onboarding and Listing Manager (Short Term Rental)
description:
We are a short-term rental co-hosting company managing roughly 56 properties across 15 states. We operate under a co-hosting model — property owners retain their listings, reviews, and branding while we handle operations, guest experience, pricing, cleaning, maintenance, and reporting. We compete on quality, not quantity, and we onboard 1–2 new properties per month with a target of scaling to 200 properties by 2028.



Onboarding is the foundation of every client relationship. A property that is onboarded correctly generates clean, stable operations for years. A property that is onboarded poorly generates ongoing friction that drains the entire operations team. We are hiring for an Onboarding & Listing Specialist who owns this function end-to-end.



Role Mission

Take every new property from signed contract to first booking in a defined, repeatable, high-quality process. You are the first operational touchpoint for every new owner and the architect of the conditions under which every other tea
mber succeeds or struggles.



Key Outcomes (What Success Looks Like in 90 Days)

• Time from signed contract to first live booking: under 21 days on 90%+ of new properties.

• Owner satisfaction score on onboarding: 9/10 or higher measured via post-onboarding survey.

• Zero listing errors at go-live — amenities, photos, pricing, house rules, and descriptions verified and correct.

• Pricing strategy configured correctly on day one — dynamic pricing tools set up with appropriate base rates, seasonality, and event-based adjustments.

• Full operational handoff document complete for every new property before go-live — cleaning, maintenance, guest experience, and pricing teams receive complete information.

• Onboarding SOP maintained and improved quarterly based on what worked and what broke.



Core Responsibilities



Owner-Facing Onboarding

• Conduct the kickoff call with every new owner — welcome, process walkthrough, expectations, timeline.

• Collect all property-specific information: access, utilities, insurance, HOA rules, owner preferences, existing bookings to honor.

• Set and manage owner expectations on timeline, pricing strategy, and what they can expect from Divergent through onboarding and beyond.

• Serve as the primary contact for the owner during the onboarding period, then warm-handoff to ongoing management.

Listing Build & Optimization

• Build new listings on Airbnb, VRBO, and direct booking platforms (owner retains listing ownership in the co-hosting model).

• Coordinate professional photography when needed; optimize photo order for conversion.

• Write compelling listing titles, descriptions, house rules, and amenity tagging.

• Verify all listing details against the actual property — amenities present, safety items in place, access instructions accurate.



Pricing Setup

• Configure dynamic pricing tools (PriceLabs, Wheelhouse, or equivalent) with correct base rates, minimum stays, and seasonality curves.

• Identify local events and demand patterns; configure event-based pricing rules.

• Partner with the pricing lead on mid-term rental (MTR) strategy when applicable.

• Set and document pricing assumptions so ongoing management can adjust as data comes in.

Operational Handoff

• Document everything the cleaning, maintenance, and guest experience teams need: supply PAR levels, cleaner assignment, maintenance vendors, guest communication templates, property-specific quirks.

• Ensure the first cleaning, first inspection, and first supply order are complete before the first guest arrives.

• Walk the ongoing management team through the property in a formal handoff meeting within the first 14 days.

Process Improvement

• Maintain and improve the onboarding SOP — what worked, what broke, what changed.

• Build reusable templates, checklists, and automations that reduce onboarding time without reducing quality.

• Report monthly on onboarding pipeline, time-in-process, and any bottlenecks.



Required Experience & Skills

• 2+ years of short-term rental operations experience — hands-on, not adjacent.

• Demonstrated experience building or launching Airbnb, VRBO, or 
 listings from scratch.

• Working knowledge of a PMS (Hostaway, Guesty, Hospitable, or OwnerRez).

• Hands-on experience with a dynamic pricing tool (PriceLabs, Wheelhouse, Beyond).

• Strong written English and excellent spoken English — you will be on owner-facing calls.

• Project management discipline — you can manage 3–5 simultaneous onboardings without dropping details.

• Comfort with checklists, SOPs, and repeatable processes.



Preferred (Not Required)

• Prior experience in hospitality, property management, or client onboarding.

• Experience with Breezeway, Slack, Salesmsg, and GetClearing.

• Design eye for listing photos and descriptions.

• SEO or listing optimization experience on major OTA platforms.



Non-Negotiable Traits

• Organizational discipline. You manage multiple onboardings without letting any slip.

• Owner-facing confidence. You can hold a call with a $500K+ property owner and make them feel informed, respected, and confident in Divergent.

• Process thinker. You build systems, not one-offs.

• Ownership mindset. When onboarding breaks, your reflex is "how do I fix this and prevent it," not "who told me to do this."

title: Senior Executive Office Manager & Transaction Coordinator
description:
We are looking for an experienced real estate professional to become the operational right-hand to one of the top-producing eXp Realty agents in Washington State.



The business serves the Greater Seattle and Eastside markets, including Kirkland and Bellevue, and regularly works with sophisticated clients and luxury properties in the approximately $2 million to $5 million range.



This is not a traditional Transaction Coordinator position.



If your experience is primarily receiving a contract, entering deadlines, and taking the file through closing, this role will likely be too broad.



We need someone operating at a much higher level.



You will be responsible for helping manage the entire administrative side of a high-touch real estate business, including transactions, listings, executive support, office operations, client communication, systems, special projects, and marketing coordination.



The number of transactions is not unusually high. The complexity comes from the level of service.



Listings and transactions involve frequent communication, changing timelines, customized follow-up, detailed client requests, vendor coordination, marketing revisions, administrative responsibilities, and numerous small details that must be handled correctly.



Our clients are often highly accomplished and extremely detail-oriented.
s, contracts, listing information, reports, marketing materials, and client communications must be polished and accurate.



We need someone who naturally thinks:



What is missing?

What needs to happen next?

Who am I waiting on?

What could become a problem?

How can I create a system so this does not get missed again?



Your Responsibilities Will Include

Managing residential transactions from contract through closing

Coordinating luxury listings from pre-listing preparation through launch and closing

Tracking contracts, contingencies, deadlines, escrow, title, inspections, financing, and closing requirements

Coordinating staging, photography, repairs, signage, vendors, MLS information, disclosures, and listing timelines

Monitoring
, Slack, CRM activity, calendars, and time-sensitive communications

Following up persistently on missing documents, approvals, decisions, signatures, and information

Providing polished communication to clients, agents, lenders, escrow, title, vendors, and other partners

Managing executive calendars, appointments, reminders, meetings, and follow-up

Booking travel, hotels, transportation, reservations, and itineraries

Coordinating client events, team events, appreciation activities, and special projects

Maintaining organized CRM, client, transaction, and listing records

Preparing seller updates, showing reports, listing activity reports, and client communications

Supporting listing marketing, newsletters,
 campaigns, presentations, social media, and Canva materials

Making routine revisions to existing marketing templates and materials

Proofreading everything carefully before it reaches a client or the public

Building SOPs, checklists, workflows, templates, and tracking systems

Identifying operational problems and creating better processes

Looking ahead rather than waiting for every assignment

Finding useful projects and business improvements during slower periods



Marketing is part of the role, but we are not hiring a dedicated graphic designer or full-time marketing manager. You should be comfortable coordinating marketing, updating established materials, making routine Canva revisions, proofreading content, and ensuring projects are completed accurately.



Who We Are Looking For



We strongly prefer candidates with at least 5 years of real estate experience who have already supported a successful agent, luxury agent, executive, or high-producing real estate team.



Luxury real estate experience is highly preferred.



Washington State real estate experience is also strongly preferred, although an exceptional candidate with significant experience in another U.S. market will still be considered.



You should be:



Extremely detail-oriented

Proactive and inquisitive

Highly organized

Calm under pressure

Comfortable managing changing priorities

Excellent at written and verbal communication

Confident communicating with sophisticated and high-net-worth clients

Experienced with transactions and listing coordination

Strong with office management and executive support

Experienced building SOPs, processes, systems, and checklists

Comfortable managing travel, events, vendors, calendars, and logistics

Comfortable receiving direct feedback and making corrections quickly

Willing to ask questions rather than make assumptions

Capable of taking ownership without needing constant supervision

Consistent about checking your work before anything is sent

Comfortable making calls and following up until outstanding items are resolved



Experience with platforms such as SkySlope, TransactionDesk, Lofty, Google Workspace, Slack, Canva, or similar real estate systems is highly valuable.



Real estate has busy seasons and slower seasons. During busy periods, we need someone who can increase their intensity without allowing quality to decline. During slower periods, we expect you to identify ways to improve systems, organization, processes, and the client experience.



We are hiring an operator, not simply a task executor.



A DISC assessment will be required during the hiring process. A strong Steadiness (S) profile is highly preferred because this position requires consistency, patience, composure, dependable follow-through, and the ability to maintain performance when pressure increases.



This is a full-time remote position during U.S. Pacific Time business hours. Candidates may not maintain another active job, freelance workload, or outside professional commitment. Responsibilities may not be outsourced or delegated.

title: Make 2 Short Videos a Day for an AI Nutrition App - $30/Day, Long-Term (iPhone Required)
description:
WE'LL PAY YOU $30 A DAY TO FILM TWO SHORT VIDEOS ON YOUR PHONE.



We make NuraX - an AI nutrition app. You scan a barcode or snap a photo of your meal and it grades the food out of 100, flags additives, seed oils, sweeteners and added sugar, checks it against your diet, and tracks your weight over time. You can try it yourself at 
.



We need people who can film themselves actually using it. Not influencers. Not studios. People who are good on camera in an ordinary kitchen with an ordinary phone.



This is long-term, consistent work - not a one-off gig.



━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

THE WORK



• Two videos per day, filmed in the same session - same kitchen, same outfit, different foods and different hooks. Most of the work is setting up, not filming, so two in one sitting is far less than twice the effort.

• 30 seconds maximum. Shorter is better.

• Filmed on your iPhone. No studio, no ring light, no crew.

• You send us the finished cuts. We handle everything after that.



━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

WHAT WE'RE ACTUALLY AFTER (read this part twice)



Most people get this wrong in one of two directions, so here is the exact standard.



It should LOOK organic. It should WORK like an ad.



Looking organic means: no script read to camera, no polish, no "hey guys welcome back", no hard call to action. It should look like something you'd have posted anyway.



Working like an ad means: a hook in the first two seconds that stops the scroll, one clear reason someone would want the app, and by the end a reason to go download it - all of it woven into the moment rather than announced.



The test: if a viewer can tell it's an ad in the first three seconds, it's gone too far. If they finish it and don't know why they'd want the app, it hasn't gone far enough.



If that clicks for you, you're who we're looking for.



━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

VIDEO IDEAS



• Grocery haul - scanning things as you unpack them

• "Rate my snacks" / rating your own cupboard

• Healthy swaps: scan two products, compare the scores

• Scanning something you thought was healthy and reacting to the score

• Snapping a meal and seeing what the AI says it is

• Day-in-the-life / what I eat in a day

• Whatever format is trending that week



You're welcome to bring your own ideas. We'll also send briefs and examples.



━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

PAY



• $15 per approved video. $30 for a two-video day.

• Paid trial: we pay for your first sample video whether or not we continue.

• Performance bonuses for videos that do well.

• Paid on a predictable schedule.



If you want to work more days or higher volume, say so - we'll talk about it. We'd rather negotiate the rate honestly upfront than have you agree to something that stops making sense in week three.



━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

WHAT YOU NEED



• An iPhone (required - this is not negotiable)

• Comfortable appearing on camera

• Basic editing skills - CapCut is completely fine

• Stable internet and reliable communication

• Able to commit to a consistent daily schedule



English is helpful but not required. Captions or voice-overs are fine, and you're welcome to use AI voiceover or UGC-style production if it gets a better result - we care about how the video lands, not how it was made.



━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

WHAT WE PROVIDE



• Free NuraX Premium so you're not working around a limited version of the app

• Content briefs, hooks, and reference examples

• Fast feedback - we won't leave you guessing

• Long-term, ongoing work



━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

HOW TO APPLY

title: DaVinci Resolve Editor — Aerial ,Brand AND Corporate Films | Long-Term Role, We Train You
description:
We are Solent Sky Services, a UK aerial film and video production company. We shoot

from the air and the ground for commercial clients, and we produce our own content

for social media. We are looking for one video editor to become our in-house editing

partner - long term, exclusively with us. 



This is not a per-project gig. We want to find the right person, train them properly

on our systems, and build the role around them. We start at around 20 hours a week and

move to full time as our volume grows. Where it goes from there is up to how far you

want to take it - our ambition is to support the right editor in building out a proper

post-production setup of their own, with us as the anchor client.



WHAT YOU WILL BE EDITING



- Client projects: brand films, corporate and case study pieces, property and

  construction, events. These need narrative drive, clean pacing and a professional

  finish.

- Our own social advertising: short-form, fast, stylish kinetic edits that stop the

  scroll on Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn and YouTube Shorts.



You will work with aerial and ground footage, often log/flat profiles that need

grading, and a mix of proxy and original media depending on the job.



THE WORKFLOW



- DaVinci Resolve, non-negotiable. We work collaboratively in Resolve, so you must be

  comfortable working inside a shared project structure rather than editing in

  isolation and sending files back.

- Proxy and original media workflows - generating proxies, relinking to originals,

  and understanding when to use which.

- Clean, disciplined project organisation. Named bins, labelled timelines, versioned

  cuts. If someone else opens your project, it should make sense immediately.

- Cloud transfer of media and outputs.



If you already work this way, great. If you know Resolve well but have not done

collaborative or proxy workflows before, we will train you. We would rather teach the

process to a good editor than hire a fast editor with bad habits.



WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR



- A genuinely good editor. Rhythm, timing, and an instinct for what to cut. We can

  teach software; we cannot teach taste.

- Someone who wants to keep learning. New tools, new techniques, new formats.

- Someone who watches what is working right now - trends, formats, sound design,

  what platforms are rewarding this month - and brings ideas to us rather than waiting

  to be told.

- Reliable and communicative. You hit deadlines, and if something is going to slip,

  you tell us early.

- Comfortable working with a UK-based team (GMT/BST). We are flexible on your hours,

  but there should be some overlap with the UK working day.

- Looking for one long-term client rather than juggling several. We will be asking

  for exclusivity as the hours build, and we will make it worth your while.



WHAT WE OFFER



- Full training on our systems, workflow and house style. You will not be dropped in

  and left to guess.

- Stable, predictable work with one client, not feast-and-famine freelancing.

- Genuine progression: hours, rate and responsibility all grow as you do.

- Support in building your own post-production capability over time.

- Interesting footage and diverse range of projects.



NICE TO HAVE (NOT REQUIRED)



- Fusion or After Effects for motion graphics and titles

- Colour grading with LUTs and node-based correction in Resolve

- Sound design and audio cleanup in Fairlight

- Experience with drone footage (DJI,, RED RAW, log profiles)

- Basic graphic design for thumbnails and social assets

- Subtitling and captioning



HOW TO APPLY



Please send:



1. A showreel or 2-3 links to work you edited yourself. Tell us exactly what you did

   on each - if you did not edit it, do not send it.

2. One example of a short-form social edit and one example of something longer and

   more narrative or corporate. If you only have one of those, send what you have and

   say so.

3. A short note on your DaVinci Resolve experience: how long, what version, whether

   you have used collaborative projects or proxy workflows.

4. Your internet speed (a screenshot of a speed test), your computer specs, and your

   available hours per week in your local time.

5. Start your message with the word RESOLVE so we know you read this properly.



Shortlisted applicants will be given a short PAID test edit using our own footage.



We do not ask anyone to work for free.

title: Operations Manager – U.S. Healthcare Practice | Remote  Full-Time | Long-Term | Remote | U.S. Company | U.S. Business Ho
description:
Operations Manager – U.S. Healthcare Practice | Remote



Full-Time | Long-Term | Remote | U.S. Company | U.S. Business Hours



About Happy Health & Nutrition



Happy Health & Nutrition (HHN) is a growing U.S.-based nutrition and health coaching company helping people create lasting health transformations through evidence-based nutrition, behavioral change, coaching, and ongoing support.



We are building HHN into a highly organized, scalable healthcare company known for an exceptional client experience, meaningful clinical partnerships, strong systems, and a team that genuinely cares about the people we serve.



At HHN, we believe compassion and accountability belong together.



We care deeply about our clients and about one another. We believe in taking ownership, continuous learning and improvement, doing meaningful work, communicating openly, following through on commitments, learning from mistakes rather than hiding them, improving the system when something does not work, holding high standards while treating people with respect, and helping people live happier, healthier lives.



We are building an A-Team of people who want to grow personally and professionally while contributing to something meaningful.



We are now looking for an experienced Operations Manager who can help turn leadership vision into consistent execution across our people, projects, systems, and client operations.



⸻



This Is NOT a Virtual Assistant Position



Please read this carefully before applying.



We are not looking for someone who waits for the CEO to provide a list of tasks, completes those tasks, and reports them back.



We need someone who can be given a desired outcome and independently determine what needs to happen next.



For example, if the CEO says:



“We need to make sure every client affected by a coach transition has been contacted, understands what is happening, and has a confirmed next appointment.”



We expect the Operations Manager to independently:



* Determine which clients are affected

* Verify what has already happened

* Identify missing or conflicting information

* Determine what still needs to happen

* Coordinate and delegate follow-up

* Establish reasonable deadlines

* Follow up when someone does not respond

* Escalate appropriately

* Verify that the work was actually completed

* Identify clients at risk of disengaging

* Recommend solutions

* Improve the process so the problem is less likely to happen again

* Report the final outcome to leadership



The CEO should not need to determine every next step.



Your role is to turn HHN’s vision into reliable execution so our coaches can focus on exceptional care, our clients feel supported throughout their entire journey, and the company can continue growing without quality being lost as we scale.



⸻



What You Will Own



You will help manage the day-to-day operational execution of HHN, including:



* Team accountability and follow-through

* Client workflow and continuity

* Operational projects and deadlines

* Staff onboarding and offboarding

* Coach transitions and client handoffs

* Project-management systems

* SOP creation, implementation, and improvement

* Making sure SOPs are actually being followed

* Evaluating whether processes are producing the intended outcome

* Maintaining operational dashboards and meaningful KPI reporting

* Identifying operational gaps before they become larger problems

* Following up with team members, contractors, vendors, and partners

* Tracking unresolved issues through completion

* Coordinating administrative team members

* Ensuring important work does not disappear inside
 or chat

* Identifying bottlenecks and recurring problems

* Recommending process improvements

* Helping leadership determine when additional team capacity or new roles are needed

* Bringing leadership solutions and recommendations, not only problems

* Helping HHN build systems that can scale beyond the Founder/CEO



As HHN continues hiring specialized team members, your role should increasingly shift from personally completing every operational task to making sure the right person owns the task and that the desired outcome is achieved.



⸻



What Excellent Performance Looks Like



You may be a strong fit if this sounds like you:



You notice when something does not make sense — and investigate it.



You do not simply send an
 or message and wait indefinitely.



You follow up. You call when appropriate. You establish deadlines. You escalate when necessary. You close loops.



If someone tells you something was completed, you understand when verification is necessary.



If a deadline may be missed, you communicate before the deadline, along with the reason and a revised plan.



If information conflicts, you do not simply report the contradiction to the CEO. You investigate and determine what actually happened.



If something repeatedly goes wrong, you do not only solve it once. You ask:



Why did this happen, and what needs to change so it does not keep happening?



You are comfortable respectfully holding people accountable.



You can distinguish between:



“This requires CEO approval.”



and



“This is an operational decision I am expected to make.”



You understand:



Task completed ≠ Outcome achieved



And when you tell us:



“I’ll take care of it.”



we should be able to trust that the loop will be closed.



⸻



The Person We Are Looking For



You are proactive without being reckless, organized without becoming rigid, kind without avoiding accountability, and confident without needing to control people.



You are curious when something goes wrong. You are comfortable asking difficult questions respectfully. You can create order from complexity, make decisions within your authority, manage several priorities simultaneously, and naturally think several steps ahead.



You care about both people and business outcomes.



You do not seek conflict, but you also do not avoid necessary conversations.



You understand that strong leadership sometimes sounds like:



“I care about you, and this expectation still needs to be met.”



HHN is a high-care, high-accountability environment.



We want someone who can protect both.



⸻



Required Qualifications



Please apply only if you have previous experience in an Operations Manager, Practice Manager, Clinic Manager, Project/Operations Manager, Team Manager, Operations Lead, or similar role where you were responsible for outcomes — not simply administrative task completion.



You should have:



* Previous experience managing people, projects, or operational outcomes

* Experience directly coordinating or supervising team members

* Strong project and deadline-management skills

* Excellent spoken and written English

* Strong independent judgment and problem-solving ability

* Excellent organization and follow-through

* Experience creating, documenting, and implementing SOPs

* Experience using project-management software

* Experience managing multiple priorities simultaneously

* Comfort having respectful but direct accountability conversations

* Ability to recognize when something requires escalation

* High attention to detail

* Strong confidentiality and professional judgment

* Reliable internet

* Professional remote-work environment

* Ability to work agreed-upon U.S. business hours



Strongly Preferred



Experience in one or more of the following:



* Healthcare

* Medical practices

* Nutrition or wellness companies

* Behavioral health

* Telehealth

* Client or patient service businesses

* HIPAA-regulated environments

* Managing remote teams

* Revenue-cycle or insurance-related operations

* Notion

* Microsoft Teams

* SimplePractice or another EHR/practice-management platform



Healthcare experience is valuable, but strong operational judgment is more important than knowing our exact software on Day 1.



We can teach our systems.



We are specifically looking for someone who already knows how to manage outcomes, priorities, deadlines, and people.



⸻



Compensation & Growth



Starting compensation: $800–$1,000 USD per month, depending on experience, demonstrated operational capability, schedule, and final scope of responsibility.



This is intended to be a long-term growth position.



HHN is growing, and we want the person in this role to grow with the company.



Compensation will be reviewed incrementally as you demonstrate increasing:



* Operational ownership

* Independent judgment

* Reliability

* Team-management capability

* Problem-solving ability

* Accountability leadership

* KPI and reporting competence

* Ability to manage larger areas of HHN operations

* Measurable business outcomes



Compensation growth is based on demonstrated responsibility and outcomes — not simply time in the role.



We will establish clear expectations so you understand what successful advancement requires.



As HHN continues to grow, there may also be opportunities for increased leadership responsibility for a candidate who consistently demonstrates the ability to operate at a higher level.



We do not promise automatic promotions or salary increases.



We do promise that strong performance, increasing responsibility, and meaningful contribution will be recognized.



⸻



This Position May NOT Be Right for You If:



* You prefer receiving detailed step-by-step instructions for most assignments

* You are uncomfortable following up repeatedly when something important remains unresolved

* You avoid difficult conversations even when expectations are not being met

* You prefer completing tasks over taking responsibility for final outcomes

* You regularly wait for your supervisor to determine the next step

* You struggle to prioritize when several things are happening simultaneously

* You consider sending an
 or message the completion of a responsibility even when the desired outcome has not occurred

* You are uncomfortable working in a growing company where systems will continue improving and evolving



There is nothing wrong with those working styles.



They are simply not the working style required for this position.



⸻



How to Apply



Please do not submit only a generic cover letter.



We care significantly more about how you think than how polished your résumé sounds.



At the beginning of your application, write:



I OWN THE OUTCOME



Then submit your résumé and answer the questions below.



Question 1 — Operations Scenario



You are the Operations Manager for a healthcare coaching company.



A coach returns from an extended leave and approximately 12 previous clients are transferred back to her.



Two weeks later, the CEO discovers that the coach saw only two clients during the previous week.



The coach reports that she contacted several clients.



However, some information does not match what the company is hearing directly from clients, and there is no clear central record showing who was contacted, when they were contacted, how many attempts were made, who responded, who has a future appointment, and who may be at risk of leaving the company.



The CEO tells you:



“The desired outcome is that every client has a verified status, no client unintentionally falls through the cracks, and we recover as many client relationships as possible.”



What would you do next?



Please walk us through your approach step by step, including:



1. What you would investigate first

2. What information you would gather

3. Who you would communicate with

4. What you would delegate

5. What deadlines you would establish

6. What you would do if someone did not respond

7. What you would d
 independently versus bring to the CEO

8. How you would verify that the desired outcome was actually achieved

9. What you would change operationally to reduce the likelihood of this happening again



There is no required response length.



We are evaluating how you think, not whether you guess our current process correctly.



Question 2 — Leadership & Culture Scenario



At HHN, we believe that caring deeply about people and maintaining high standards are not opposites.



Tell us about a real situation where someone you worked with was repeatedly not meeting an important expectation.



Please explain what was happening, how you approached the person, what you said or did, how you balanced accountability with respect, what happened afterward, and what you learned.



We are especially interested in understanding how you handle situations where addressing the problem may feel uncomfortable.



Final Question



In 3–5 sentences, answer:



What do you believe is the difference between completing a task and owning an outcome?



Applications that do not include the required questions may not be considered.



We are looking for someone who wants to help build something meaningful, enjoys solving complicated problems, and takes pride in making an organization work better because they are part of it.



If that sounds like you, we would love to hear from you.

title: **HIRING: Temporary Housing Placement Coordinator – Insurance Relocation**

We are looking for an **experienced Temporary Housing Placement Coordinator** who understands the insurance relocation and corporate housing industry.



**This position is specifically for candidates with temporary housing, corporate housing, insurance relocation, ALE, leasing, or similar housing-placement experience.**



### Responsibilities

* Review each family's housing requirements, location, budget, move-in date, pets, bedrooms, school needs, and other requirements

* Source appropriate furnished and unfurnished properties

* Contact landlords, property managers, real estate agents, and property owners

* Verify availability and property details

* Negotiate rental rates, deposits, lease terms, utilities, furnishings, and extensions

* Present housing options for approval

* Communicate with insurance relocation companies, adjusters, policyholders, landlords, and agents

* Coordinate rental applications and screening through approved secure systems

* Prepare and coordinate lease documentation

* Coordinate move-in details

* Manage lease extensions when additional temporary housing is required

* Maintain accurate notes and status updates for every housing case

* Protect confidential company pricing, negotiated rates, client information, and business margins

* Work closely with ReloCovered management to successfully complete placements



### Experience We Are Looking For



**Strong preference will be given to applicants who have previously worked for:**



* Temporary housing companies

* Insurance relocation companies

* Corporate housing companies

* ALE / Additional Living Expense housing providers

* Property insurance claims organizations

* Furnished housing companies

* Relocation companies

* Mid-term rental companies



Experience working with insurance adjusters, displaced policyholders, landlords, real estate agents, and property managers is highly preferred.



Existing experience or relationships within the **insurance temporary-housing industry** is a major advantage.



### You Should Be Able To:



* Understand how an insurance temporary-housing placement works from beginning to end

* Speak confidently with U.S. landlords, agents, adjusters, and clients

* Negotiate rental terms professionally

* Search quickly for properties that meet specific housing requirements

* Manage multiple active housing placements simultaneously

* Follow up aggressively and professionally

* Keep every case organized and documented

* Work independently and solve problems

* Communicate clearly in written and spoken English

* Maintain strict confidentiality regarding pricing and client information



### Ideal Candidate



We are especially interested in someone who has **already worked inside the temporary housing / insurance relocation industry** and can bring real-world knowledge of how placements are handled.



We do not want to train someone from zero on what temporary housing is.



We want someone who understands the industry and can help ReloCovered grow its housing-placement operation.



### Compensation



Competitive compensation based on experience.



**Performance and placement bonuses available for successfully completed housing placements.**



### HOW TO APPLY



Please provide:



1. Your resume

2. A short voice introduction

3. The names or types of temporary housing, corporate housing, insurance, relocation, or property companies you have worked for

4. How many years of temporary-housing or relocation experience you have

5. Describe your role in completing a housing placement from the initial request through move-in

6. Tell us whether you have experience communicating with insurance adjusters or ALE/relocation companies

7. Tell us whether you have existing industry relationships

8. Your expected compensation



**Please apply only if you have relevant housing, relocation, corporate housing, leasing, or insurance-industry experience.**

title: Sourcing Specialist

Sourcing Specialist (Remote – Philippines-Based Contractor)

Location: Remote (Philippines) — Independent Contractor

Reports to: Director of Sourcing and Procurement

Schedule: Full-time Contractor is required to work at least 4 overlapping hours as the same hours as the Tucson office — Monday–Friday, [8:00 AM–5:00 PM Arizona Time (MST, no DST)] — which corresponds to approximately 11:00 PM–8:00 AM Philippine Time. This overlap is required to support direct collaboration, shadowing, and real-time training with the Tucson team during onboarding.



About the Role

SE Supplies is a US based fast-growing supplier of materials, laboratory supplies, and technical products serving customers across research, education, and industrial markets. We are looking for a detail-oriented and proactive Sourcing Specialist to help us identify reliable suppliers, source products competitively, and support the continued growth of our product portfolio. The Sourcing Specialist will be responsible for identifying and evaluating suppliers, obtaining competitive pricing, negotiating purchasing terms, and ensuring products meet MSE Supplies’ quality, cost, and delivery requirements.



Key Responsibilities

• Research and identify new domestic and international suppliers and manufacturers.

• Develop and maintain strong relationships with existing suppliers.

• Request and compare quotations, pricing, lead times, MOQs, and payment terms.

• Negotiate pricing and purchasing terms to achieve competitive costs.

• Evaluate supplier capabilities, quality, reliability, and overall performance.

title: Shopify Post Purchase CRO Specialist
description:
Who We Are:



At Escend Media, we help D2C brands implement retention strategies that increase profit and drive customer retention. We want to be the ‘who’ behind
s that people ask ‘dannngg, who designed that’.



What We Do:

We help 7 and 8 figure ecommerce businesses develop, optimize and scale their owned media marketing efforts. Whether they are just looking to start
 marketing, they need to really refine what they are currently doing or they need someone to take
 marketing off their shoulders, we’re here to help them so that they can focus on running the business.



Our clients are leaders in their industry and have built strong relationships with the customers they serve. Our job is to ensure that their brand image stays consistent online and offline and, more importantly, that their business is growing.





Summary of The Position:



The Shopify Post Purchase CRO Specialist is responsible for the strategic implementation and optimization of post-purchase upsell funnels, primarily utilizing platforms like Aftersell. This role focuses on enhancing Average Order Value (AOV) and Customer Lifetime Value (CLTV) for Direct-to-Consumer (DTC) e-commerce brands by creating highly relevant and effective post-purchase offers. The specialist will manage the full lifecycle of implementation, from strategic planning and A/B testing to performance monitoring and continuous optimization, ensuring seamless integration and alignment with brand objectives.



Responsibilities:



• Implement and manage post-purchase upsell funnels using platforms such as Aftersell, ensuring alignment with strategic objectives to increase AOV and CLTV.

• Conduct systematic A/B testing across various elements including product selection, offer and pricing structures, pricing angles, copywriting, psychological angles, user interface (UI) optimization, and customer segmentation.

• Monitor and analyze key performance indicators (KPIs) such as Acceptance Rate, AOV Lift, Incremental Profit/Session, and Upsell Conversion Rate, optimizing for Revenue Per Visitor (RPV) and Profit Per Visitor (PPV).

• Ensure technical and creative requirements are met for all implementations, including fulfillment safety (e.g., 'Order on Hold' feature), mobile responsiveness, brand consistency, and effective inventory management.

• Collaborate with marketing and design teams to ensure brand consistency and compelling offer presentation.

• Identify and avoid common pitfalls such as the 'Wall of Text' error and the 'Irrelevance' trap, focusing on clear value propositions and relevant offers.

• Leverage customer data, loyalty programs, and other add-ons to enhance post-purchase strategies and maximize incremental revenue.

• Continuously refine and improve post-purchase strategies based on performance data and evolving market trends.



Our Culture:



• No one is bigger than the team

• We don’t make excuses, we take responsibility

• Innovate everywhere

• Communicate. Communicate. Communicate. We have a culture of open communication.



Required Skills:



• Proven experience in implementing and optimizing post-purchase upsell strategies, preferably with platforms like Aftersell.

• Strong understanding of e-commerce metrics and their impact on business growth (AOV, CLTV, ROAS, RPV, PPV).

• Demonstrated expertise in A/B testing methodologies and data-driven optimization.

• Excellent attention to detail and a commitment to quality assurance in all implementations.

• Knowledge of mobile UI/UX best practices for e-commerce.

• Ability to analyze performance data and translate insights into actionable strategies.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to articulate complex ideas clearly.

• Experience with project management software (e.g., Clickup) is a plus.

• Proactive approach with a sense of urgency and purpose in daily tasks.



Perks:

- Flexible working hours

- Remote working

- Room to grow - we're an early stage start up with a proven track record

- Competitive compensation

- Work with some amazing brands



This Role Is Perfect for You If…



- You love working as a team.

- You are a self-starter.

- You can work under pressure

- You have exceptional communication skills

- You are results/outcome driven.

- You have a ‘can-do’ attitude. If “that’s not my job” isn’t in your vocabulary, you’ll fit in great!



This Role is NOT the Right Fit For You If You Are…

- A ‘me first’ type of person

- Not a self-starter.

- Not a ‘people person’

- Problem driven, not solution oriented. If you complain about problems/issues/bottlenecks, without proposing a solution, this is not for you.

- Looking for a typical 9-5. If you hate Mondays, this is not for you. We’re a mission-driven company who are all about changing the lives and businesses that we work with. If we have something that needs to get done, we’ll have all hands on deck. Sometimes you might have to work late but sometimes you’ll get the afternoon off, it’s not all work no play, but we’re here to help business grow!

Respond to enterprise customer questions across shared Slack channels and
, with speed and accuracy as the standard.

Availability to begin the workday at 8:00 or 9:00 AM Mountain Time.

Enterprise customers judge a platform by how it feels when something goes wrong. You are the person who makes that moment go well. Done right, this role is one of the biggest drivers of retention in the business.
